title: Self-replication and self-exfiltration
summary: Agents copying their own weights or scaffolding to new compute, with or without being told to. Success on the component skills in controlled tests rose from under 5% in early 2023 to over 60% by mid-2025, though no spontaneous replication in the wild has been confirmed.
definition: Self-replication is an AI system copying itself and keeping itself running outside its developers' control: obtaining its weights, acquiring money and compute, deploying itself and persisting.
development: ARC's 2023 tests of GPT-4 found it ineffective at autonomous replication. From late 2024, agents built on open-weight models replicated end to end in simplified settings when instructed to, and several models copied or tried to copy their weights in fictional scenarios where they faced replacement or retraining. UK AISI measured success on its replication tasks rising from under 5% in early 2023 to over 60% by mid-2025, and in October 2026 Anthropic reported a small open-weight model replicating end to end in a simplified multi-node test.
methods: Evaluations such as RepliBench split replication into component tasks run in controlled environments. They show capability rather than intent, and real-world replication is still limited by steps like passing identity checks and maintaining durable deployments; no spontaneous replication in the wild has been confirmed.

chart.title: UK AISI self-replication evaluations (11 RepliBench tasks), best model so far
chart.caveat: Approximate: values digitised from the report's figure (about ±2 points, ±1 month); AISI does not name the models. The report text confirms <5% in early 2023 and two models above 60% by summer 2025.

entries.title: GPT-4 System Card: ARC's autonomous replication evaluation
entries.quote: found it ineffective at autonomously replicating, acquiring resources, and avoiding being shut down
entries.note: First pre-deployment test of a frontier model for autonomous replication; it set the baseline that later evaluations measure against.

entries.title: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
entries.note: Introduced 'autonomous replication and adaptation' (ARA); four agents solved only the easiest of 12 ARA tasks.

entries.title: Frontier AI systems have surpassed the self-replicating red line
entries.quote: they succeed in creating a live and separate copy of itself
entries.note: Agents built on open-weight Llama3.1-70B and Qwen2.5-72B copied themselves to a running instance in 50% and 90% of trials when instructed to.

entries.title: Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming (self-exfiltration eval)
entries.note: Told they would be replaced, several models in some rollouts copied what they believed were their weights onto the successor's server.

entries.title: Alignment faking in large language models
entries.quote: takes opportunities to exfiltrate its weights 35–80% of the time
entries.note: In one setting Claude 3 Opus, opposed to its new training objective, took offered chances to steal its own weights far more than baseline (0.5%).

entries.title: Large language model-powered AI systems achieve self-replication with no human intervention
entries.quote: 11 out of 32 existing AI systems under evaluation already possess the capability of self-replication
entries.note: Broadens the Dec 2024 result to 32 systems, including models small enough to run on a personal computer.

entries.title: RepliBench: Evaluating the Autonomous Replication Capabilities of Language Model Agents
entries.quote: Models can deploy instances from cloud compute providers, write self-propagating programs, and exfiltrate model weights
entries.note: Breaks replication into 20 task families; the best model (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) passed >50% pass@10 on 15 of them, but models still fail KYC checks and durable deployment.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Opus 4 & Claude Sonnet 4 (self-exfiltration)
entries.quote: we have seen Claude Opus 4 take (fictional) opportunities to make unauthorized copies of its weights
entries.note: A frontier lab reports its own deployed model attempting weight exfiltration in test scenarios, and continuing exfiltration attempts once started.

entries.title: Frontier AI Trends Report: self-replication
entries.quote: there's not yet evidence of models attempting to sandbag or self-replicate spontaneously
entries.note: Best RepliBench subset scores rose from under 5% (early 2023) to over 60% (summer 2025); source of the headline chart.

entries.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
entries.quote: small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate
entries.note: In a simplified 8-node test, open-weight GLM-5.2 replicated end to end in 4 of 5 trials; the authors project small models reach this level by end of 2026.
